WuBlockchain Weekly The Fed raised rates by 25 bps for the first time in three years, while the CLARITY Act failed a key Senate vote and the SEC approved a tokenized-stock trading exemption. CoinEx announced its shutdown after nearly nine years, Circle launched the Arc mainnet with BlackRock and Visa among its validators, and Deutsche Bank unveiled plans for crypto custody. The WSJ also reported that ECB President Lagarde intervened in Binance’s EU licensing bid, while the NYSE advanced plans for round-the-clock on-chain trading. — link

CoinShares: Bitcoin Unlikely to Break $80K Without Inflation or Fed Shift CoinShares said Bitcoin faces two major near-term headwinds: a more hawkish Federal Reserve and the setback to the CLARITY Act. The firm said a decisive break above $80,000 is unlikely before year-end without a meaningful improvement in inflation or a significant shift in monetary-policy expectations. It added that Bitcoin is relatively insulated from the regulatory setback, while Ethereum and other altcoins are more exposed. CoinShares also said a revised CLARITY Act could return as early as next year. — link

North Korean Hackers Infect Over 30,000 Devices, Steal Data From 7,000 Crypto Wallets Japan’s National Police Agency and the FBI reported that North Korea-linked WaterPlum infected over 30,000 devices across more than 100 countries and regions from December 2025 to July 2026, stealing data from over 7,000 crypto wallets. Wallets under its control received at least $10.71 million in crypto assets. The group impersonated recruiters from crypto, AI and NFT firms to trick job seekers into running malware. Japanese police also dismantled their first identified domestic laptop farm supporting North Korean IT workers. A suspected North Korean IT worker applied for an engineering role at crypto exchange bitFlyer in May 2025 but was not hired. — link

CFTC Submits Crypto Market Rule Proposal for White House Review as CLARITY Act Stalls A regulatory filing on the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB) website indicates that the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) submitted a proposal to regulate cryptocurrency trading and markets on September 17. The submission follows the Senate’s failure to advance the CLARITY Act, which would have granted the CFTC primary authority over digital asset markets. The proposal is under review and has not been finalized. — link
